iddialar.alinti: The unfinished nature of the work reveals Michelangelo's painting technique, completing areas in turn in the manner of a fresco or tempera work, rather than sketching out the whole work and adding details, as for example Raphael or Leonardo would have done.

iddialar.iddia: Kompozisyon yenidir: defin sahnelerinde İsa'nın bedeni genellikle yatay tutulurken, Michelangelo'yu etkilemiş olabileceği düşünülen önceki dikey örnekler arasında Fra Angelico'nun San Marco Altarpiece'ine ait 1438-1440 predellası ve Domenico Ghirlandaio vardır.
iddialar.alinti: The composition is a novel one, with the body of Jesus typically held horizontally in paintings of the Entombment, although earlier examples with Jesus held vertically that may have influenced Michelangelo include a 1438-1440 predella to the San Marco Altarpiece by Fra Angelico, and Domenico Ghirlandaio.

iddialar.iddia: Bazı figürlerin havada duruyormuş gibi görünmesi, kısmen tablonun aşağıdan bakılmak üzere tasarlanmış olmasından ve bitmemiş olmasından kaynaklanıyor olabilir.
iddialar.alinti: The floating appearance of some of the figures may be partly explained by the fact that the painting is intended to be viewed from below, and to the fact that it is unfinished.

iddialar.iddia: Lapis lazuli tozundan yapılan pahalı mavi pigment ultramarinenin kıt olması, tablonun tamamlanmasını geciktirmiş ve eserin neden bitmemiş kaldığını açıklamış olabilir.
iddialar.alinti: Many of the unfinished parts of the painting, such as the cloak of the missing Virgin, would have required quantities of the expensive blue pigment ultramarine made from powdered lapis lazuli. If this was in short supply, it could be that this would have held up completion of the painting, which may explain why it was unfinished.

iddialar.alinti: However, even if this were so, it would not explain why the artist could not have completed the many other parts of the painting that did not require any blue.

iddialar.alinti: According to documents discovered in 1981, Michelangelo had been commissioned in 1500 to paint a panel for the funerary chapel at the church of Sant'Agostino in Rome, but in the end gave back the sum received.
